validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row roster and the batch's flagged 'Spire, 2 rows' cluster ('MoGas (Fort Leonard Wood MO <-> Alton/Wood River IL) changed hands before reaching Spire -- lead: CorEnergy owned it, then sold it to Spire -- verify the dates'). P2565 is a real, thoroughly documented 263-mile (423.30 km) FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipeline, confirmed by CorEnergy Infrastructure Trust's FY2022 10-K (SEC CIK 1347652, filed 2023-03-29) and Spire Inc.'s FY2025 10-K (SEC CIK 1126956, filed 2025-11-14) -- two different filers, a former owner and the current owner, describing the same physical asset consistently. Ownership chain verified: Energy Investors Fund (EIF, original owner) sold MoGas to CorEnergy Infrastructure Trust for $125 million, closed Nov 25, 2014 (PE Hub); CorEnergy then sold MoGas + the affiliated Omega Pipeline System to Spire Inc. for $176.1 million, announced 2023 (OGJ) and closed Jan 19, 2024 (Spire's own FY2025 10-K, Note 18 Business Combinations). NOT a duplicate of P0255 (Spire STL Pipeline, a physically separate 65-mile greenfield line Spire built 2018-2019 that merely interconnects with MoGas around St. Louis) -- both CorEnergy's and Spire's 10-Ks independently and consistently distinguish the two systems by name, mileage, and regulatory history. NOT a duplicate of the Omega Pipeline System either -- Omega is a separate, non-FERC-regulated 75-mile natural gas DISTRIBUTION system (not transmission) located on the Fort Leonard Wood Army post, owned by the same corporate family (Mowood/Omega under CorEnergy, then Spire) but never described by any source as part of the MoGas transmission pipeline itself; it does not appear to carry its own GEM gas-transmission row, which is correct given GEM's transmission-only tracker scope. See the attribution concerns below (Owner/Operator name staleness; StartLocation precision) and the status_review/cross_row_lead entries for the major Jan 1, 2026 FERC-approved administrative merger of P0255 into P2565's certificate.

MoGas was not built as a single greenfield 'proposed' project -- per the mogaspipe.com pipeline-background page (archived, see Start fill below), it was formed in 2008 by the COMBINATION of three already-existing, already-operating affiliated pipeline systems (Missouri Interstate Gas, Missouri Gas Company, Missouri Pipeline Company), two of which (MGC, MPC) were already intrastate pipelines regulated by the Missouri Public Service Commission before 2008, and one (MIG) was already an operating interstate pipeline. I could not find any source describing a discrete 'proposal' date or filing for this 2008 combination distinct from the formation/start date itself -- searched CorEnergy's FY2022 10-K, Spire's FY2025 10-K, the EIA pipeline-projects workbook (which lists only post-2008 MoGas-related expansion projects, not the original 2008 formation), OGJ, and PE Hub; none give a proposal date. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than guess or duplicate the Start value.

Same reasoning as Proposal: the 2008 formation was a corporate combination of three pre-existing, already-built pipeline systems, not new-build construction with its own discrete construction-start date. The EIA workbook's 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' sheet DOES document a later, separate, sourced project on this system -- the 'Curryville Compression Expansion Project,' operator 'MoGas Energy LLC,' $16.1 million, FERC Docket CP07-450, completed 2009-03-20 -- but that is a post-formation COMPRESSOR expansion, not the original system's construction, so I am not using it to fill ConstructionYear (it would misattribute a partial 2009 expansion as the system's founding construction). No source gives a construction-start date for the original three predecessor systems or their 2008 combination. Leaving UNRESOLVED.

cross_row_leads.lead: P0255's own staged shard (already in this staging dir) flags the Oct 8, 2025 FERC-approved abandonment-by-transfer of Spire STL's facilities into Spire MoGas as a SINGLE-SOURCED finding (thompsonenergyexpert.com, paywalled) and, on that basis, deliberately did NOT change P0255's Owner1/Operator values pending a confirmed completion date. Researching P2565 in this pass turned up two STRONGER, independently corroborating, fully citable sources for the same event that upgrade it well past single-sourced: (1) Spire's own FY2025 10-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1126956, filed 2025-11-14, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1126956/000119312525282583/sr-20250930.htm) states plainly: 'On October 8, 2025, FERC approved the merger of Spire STL Pipeline into Spire MoGas Pipeline, consolidating operations under a single certificate and tariff while maintaining existing rates and service continuity'; (2) the EIA's own Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (live at eia.gov, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx) independently describes the same event in its 'MoGas Expansion Project' entry's notes: '...Companion filing with Spire STL Pipeline (merged 1/1/2026 into a single Spire MoGas Pipeline certificate).' Recommend revisiting P0255's attribution concern with this stronger sourcing: an SEC 10-K plus a federal government database are two independent, high-tier origins, both giving a firm effective date of Jan 1, 2026 for the merger (not merely 'approved, completion date unconfirmed' as P0255's shard currently states) -- this may be enough to justify changing P0255's Owner1/Operator to 'Spire MoGas Pipeline LLC' effective 2026-01-01, or at minimum upgrading the concern's tier from medium to high with the completion date now confirmed. Also note: spireenergy.com's own current MoGas pipeline page states a combined system length of approximately 328 miles (263 mi MoGas + 65 mi Spire STL/P0255), consistent with -- not contradicting -- the two systems' pre-merger individually-documented lengths; this is the post-merger COMBINED-CERTIFICATE figure, not evidence that either individual pipeline's own historical mileage (263 mi for P2565, 65 mi for P0255) was wrong.
